mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% year-over-year signals inflationary pressures that typically lead to tighter monetary policy, which in turn negatively impacts S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPI YoY > 2% does not correlate with subsequent tightening actions by the Fed.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in one month signals a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 70% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between UNRATE spikes and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in Real Final Sales (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or RSAFS decline does not precede a significant downturn in economic activity (GDP growth remains positive).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in Industrial Production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a single month signals a surge in economic activity, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between INDPRO spikes and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 5% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is rising, the combination signals a tightening monetary policy and inflationary pressures, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in a multivariate regression model.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over three consecutive months signals a strengthening demand for housing, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between HOUST increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month, the combination signals a tight labor market and strong job growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in a multivariate regression model.

mechanism_narrative: When Industrial Production (INDPRO) is declining and Real GDP (GDPC1) growth is below 2% year-over-year, the combination signals a weakening supply side of the economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in a multivariate regression model.
